scenario.name: Microsoft & CISA — Volt Typhoon: Living-off-the-Land ntdsutil IFM & netsh Portproxy
scenario.shortSubtitle: Microsoft Threat Intel / CISA AA24-038A · KV-Botnet Edge Relay, WMIC, ntds.dit & netsh
scenario.overview: Imagine a brick city apartment building entrance with a glass vestibule, a wall of brass resident mailboxes, a doorman podium, and a glowing brass intercom buzzer panel. Standing outside the locked glass apartment vestibule, an uninvited caller presses a crafted sequence on the brass intercom buzzer pretending to be building maintenance. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station, then moves quietly past the locked glass vestibule door into neighboring restricted rooms. The doorman checks the visitor sign-in ledger against the intercom buzz history and realizes no maintenance visit was ever scheduled by management. In this scenario (T1003.003, Microsoft & CISA, Volt Typhoon: Living-off-the-Land ntdsutil IFM & netsh Portproxy) on SRV-MGMT-01 (10.10.15), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: routing Through KV-Botnet SOHO Routers, then using Built-in ntdsutil.exe to Dump Every, then multi-Hop Internal Relay via netsh interface. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Routing Through KV-Botnet SOHO Routers, then Using Built-in ntdsutil.exe to Dump Every, then Multi-Hop Internal Relay via netsh interface, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: HANDS-ON-KEYBOARD WMI DISCOVERY & LATERAL EXEC
stages.subtitle: wmic process call create across Domain Controller and management hosts
stages.description: Standing outside the locked glass apartment vestibule, an uninvited caller presses a crafted sequence on the brass intercom buzzer pretending to be building maintenance. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station while everyday visitors and the building doorman go about their routine. Instead of connecting from a rented cloud VPS that threat-intelligence feeds would block, the attacker connects through a compromised small-office/home-office (SOHO) router in the same geographic region (KV-Botnet node 198.51.100.14, so geo-IP filters see normal local ISP traffic) into the IT Jump Server SRV-MGMT-01 (10.10.15.22). From SRV-MGMT-01, the operator executes wmic /node:10.10.0.5 process call create "cmd.exe /Q /c ntdsutil "ac i ntds" "ifm"..." toward Domain Controller CORP-DC01 (10.10.0.5), causing WmiPrvSE.exe on CORP-DC01 to spawn the command under PID 6412 and return ReturnValue = 0 (confirming remote process creation over DCOM/RPC without dropping any third-party remote-execution binary). When wmic.exe connects over TCP/135 (RPC Endpoint Mapper) and dynamic DCOM ports to CORP-DC01 (10.10.0.5), the remote WMI provider host (WmiPrvSE.exe) spawns cmd.exe / ntdsutil.exe (PID 6412) under the authenticated administrator context (recording Sysmon Event ID 1 on CORP-DC01 with ParentImage = WmiPrvSE.exe). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ WMIC REMOTE EXEC / ⇠#1 ACK PID 6412) from Node ① (#1 KV-Botnet SOHO Edge Node) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Sentinel & MDE).

stages.title: OFFLINE NTDS.DIT EXTRACTION VIA NTDSUTIL IFM
stages.subtitle: Creating Volume Shadow Copy and dumping ntds.dit + SYSTEM hive
stages.description:
Fooled by the caller’s voice over the lobby intercom, the building doorman buzzes open the interior lobby door and reads out the hallway elevator code. Here in Step 2 inside the apartment lobby, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station without disturbing the resident locked mailboxes. Active Directory exclusively locks C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit (the master database file containing the password hashes of every employee, service, and Domain Admin in the company) while the Domain Controller is running, so normal copy commands fail. Running under PID 6412 on CORP-DC01 (10.10.0.5), ntdsutil "ac i ntds" "ifm" "create full C:\Windows\Temp	mp_ad" (where "ac i ntds" selects the Active Directory database instance, and "ifm" / "create full" instructs Microsoft’s signed backup tool to take a Volume Shadow Copy snapshot) writes an unlocked copy of C:\Windows\Temp	mp_ad\Active Directory
tds.dit plus the registry\SYSTEM decryption hive (emitting ESENT Application Event ID 325 confirming the new database file was created). The ifm (Install From Media, originally designed so administrators could promote a new Domain Controller from a backup folder) command in ntdsutil.exe (PID 6412) automatically invokes vssvc.exe to snapshot the volume, extracts both Active Directory
tds.dit and registry\SYSTEM (which holds the BootKey required to decrypt the NTLM and Kerberos keys inside ntds.dit offline), and removes the temporary shadow copy upon completion. On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ NTDS.DIT CREATED / ⇠#2 ACK Event 325) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 IT Jump Server (Netsh Proxy)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Sentinel & MDE).

stages.title: MULTI-HOP INTERNAL RELAY VIA NETSH PORTPROXY
stages.subtitle: Configuring persistent TCP port forwarding in Windows Registry
stages.description: Slipping past the brass resident mailboxes straight into the elevator, the intruder gains access to private upper-floor corridors without ever owning an apartment key. In this final step inside the apartment lobby, the intruder moves quietly past the locked glass vestibule door into neighboring restricted rooms until the doorman visitor sign-in book catches the mismatch. To maintain stealthy multi-hop access and relay staged archives out through the jump server SRV-MGMT-01 (10.10.15.22), the attacker runs C:\Windows\System32\netsh.exe (PID 6890): netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenaddress=0.0.0.0 listenport=8443 connectaddress=10.10.0.5 connectport=3389 (instructing Windows’ built-in IP Helper service to forward inbound TCP port 8443 traffic directly to CORP-DC01 at 10.10.0.5:3389 without dropping any custom proxy binary to disk). When netsh.exe (PID 6890) executes the portproxy add v4tov4 command, the Windows kernel/service configuration writes the forwarding rule into HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PortProxy\v4tov4\tcp\0.0.0.0/8443 with value 10.10.0.5/3389 (persisting the tunnel across reboots inside the native IpHlpSvc service while triggering Sysmon Event ID 13 RegistryEvent). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ NETSH PORTPROXY / ⇠#3 ACK PortProxy) from Node ③ (#3 IT Jump Server (Netsh Proxy)) to Node ④ (#4 ntdsutil.exe & vssadmin.exe), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Sentinel & MDE).

detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Ntdsutil Install From Media (IFM) NTDS.dit Dump

  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:

title: Suspicious Access to NTDS.dit via ESENT Database Engine
